Writing the answer…### Part 1: What the Law Requires
The law does not explicitly require the officer who first registers a case to be the same one who investigates it. In fact, the Code of Criminal Procedure (Pakistan) allows for flexibility in assigning roles. For example, under Section 156, any officer in charge of a police station may investigate a cognizable case without the order of a Magistrate [Document 4]. Additionally, in non-cognizable cases, a police officer may investigate only with the order of a Magistrate [Document 5]. There is no specific provision that mandates the same officer to both register and investigate a case.

### Part 2: What Our Case Records Actually Show
In our case records, the roles of the officer who recorded the FIR and the officer who investigated the case are mostly NOT separated. In 68 of 74 recorded assignment pairs (92%), the same person performed both roles. Roles are split in only 6 pairs, across 6 cases. Of these 6 split cases:
- 3 of them have an investigating officer with no recording officer on the same case at all, making the pair unresolvable rather than genuinely split [Document 6].Response generated (1127 chars)

Writing the answer…### Part 1: What the Law Requires
According to the **Code of Criminal Procedure (Pakistan)**, when a person dies while in the custody of the police, the nearest Magistrate empowered to hold inquests shall conduct an inquiry into the cause of death. This is outlined in **section 176** of the Code, which mandates that such an inquiry be held either instead of, or in addition to, the investigation held by the police-officer. The Magistrate is also given the power to disinter corpses if necessary to determine the cause of death, as stated in **section 176(2)** [Document 5].

### Part 2: What Our Case Records Show
Our case records do not specifically track whether an inquiry into the cause of death was conducted in cases where a person died while in the custody of the police. The summary of our case records shows that **10 of the 73 FIR(s)** that carry a recorded section cite **PPC §302**, which pertains to murder. However, this does not indicate whether an inquiry into the cause of death was conducted in these cases or whether the records contain any information about such inquiries [Document 7].

In conclusion, while the law mandates an inquiry into the cause of death in such cases, our records do not provide specific information on whether such inquiries were conducted in the cases where death occurred.
